lessons.title: Get ready! What you will learn

pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 🔤 **Strand 2 — Algebra**
Using letters and symbols to describe patterns, relationships and unknown quantities.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B8.2.3)
- B8.2.3.1 — Demonstrate understanding of linear inequalities of the form ax ≥ b (where a and b are integers) by modelling problems as linear inequalities and solving the problems concretely, pictorially and symbolically.

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- use the symbols <, >, ≤ and ≥ and translate word problems into linear inequalities (and vice versa)
- solve simple linear inequalities using the idea of balancing
- find solution sets of inequalities in a given domain and show them on a number line

pages.title: Key words and map
pages.body:
> ✨ **Key words**
- inequality
- less than
- greater than
- at least
- at most
- solution set
- domain
- number line

> 🗺️ **Sections in this chapter**
- 7.1 Writing inequalities
- 7.2 Solving linear inequalities
- 7.3 Solution sets in given domains

pages.title: Writing inequalities
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Translate word problems into linear inequalities in one variable and vice versa.
Curriculum indicator B8.2.3.1.1
| **Symbol** | **Meaning** | **Words that suggest it** |
|---|---|---|
| < | is less than | fewer than, below, under |
| > | is greater than | more than, above, exceeds |
| ≤ | is less than or equal to | at most, not more than, maximum |
| ≥ | is greater than or equal to | at least, not less than, minimum |
## ✏️ Example 7.1
Write an inequality for each statement.
a) Think of a whole number less than 17.
b) Eight less than the product of −3 and a number is greater than −26.
c) Kwaakye's profit for March of GH₵32 was at least GH₵12 less than his February profit p.
**Solution**
a) **x < 17** (x a whole number)
b) "The product of −3 and a number" is −3x; eight less than that is −3x − 8: **−3x − 8 > −26**
c) "At least GH₵12 less than p" means the difference p − 32 is at least 12: **p − 32 ≥ 12**, i.e. p ≥ 44. His February profit was **at least GH₵44**.
## ✏️ Example 7.2
Write a word statement for each inequality: a) x + 5 ≤ 20 b) 2n > 15 c) 100 − 7k ≥ 30
**Solution**
a) "Five more than a number is at most 20." b) "Twice a number is more than 15." c) "When 7 times a number is taken from 100, the result is at least 30."

pages.title: Exercise 7.1
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 7.1** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
1. Write an inequality: a) The temperature t was below 0 °C. b) A lift can carry at most 8 people (p). c) You must be at least 18 years old (a) to vote. d) Three times a number, increased by 4, exceeds 25.
2. A taxi can carry at most 4 passengers. Write an inequality for the number of taxis t needed to carry 22 passengers.
3. Write a word problem for: a) y − 3 < 10 b) 5m ≥ 60

pages.title: Solving linear inequalities
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Solve simple linear inequalities.
Curriculum indicator B8.2.3.1.2
> 🔑 **Key idea: Solving inequalities** — Solve an inequality like an equation, keeping it "balanced": you may add or subtract the same number on both sides, and multiply or divide both sides by the same **positive** number. **If you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number, reverse the inequality sign.**
## ✏️ Example 7.3
Why must the sign be reversed? Consider 3 < 5.
**Solution**
Multiply both sides by −1: −3 and −5. On the number line −3 is to the right of −5, so **−3 > −5**. The sign has reversed.
## ✏️ Example 7.4
Solve: a) 2x − 11 > 29 b) 4x − 9 > −5 c) 14 < 8 − 2x d) 3x ≤ 8 + x e) x − 4 > 1 f) 10 − x < 12 g) x − 3 ≥ 2 h) 4x − 5 ≤ 3x + 1
**Solution**
a) 2x > 40 ⟹ **x > 20**
b) 4x > 4 ⟹ **x > 1**
c) 14 − 8 < −2x ⟹ 6 < −2x ⟹ divide by −2 and reverse: **x < −3**
d) 2x ≤ 8 ⟹ **x ≤ 4**
e) **x > 5**
f) −x < 2 ⟹ **x > −2**
g) **x ≥ 5**
h) **x ≤ 6**
## ✏️ Example 7.5
Solve −3x − 8 > −26.
**Solution**
−3x > −18 ⟹ (divide by −3, reverse) **x < 6**

pages.title: Solution sets in given domains
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Determine solution sets of simple linear inequalities in given domains.
Curriculum indicator B8.2.3.1.3
> 🔑 **Key idea: Solution set** — The **solution set** is the set of all values in the given **domain** (e.g. whole numbers, integers) that make the inequality true. On a number line, an **open circle** (○) means the end value is **not included** (< or >); a **closed circle** (●) means it **is included** (≤ or ≥).
[[fig:m8-f20|Figure 7.1: Showing inequalities on a number line]]
## ✏️ Example 7.6
Find the solution set and illustrate it on a number line.
a) x < 4, x a whole number. b) 2x > 24, x a whole number less than 20. c) x + 4 ≤ 3x − 16, x an integer less than 15. d) 9 − 5x < 6, x an integer such that −3 ≤ x ≤ 3.
**Solution**
a) Whole numbers less than 4: **{0, 1, 2, 3}**
b) x > 12 and x < 20: **{13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19}**
c) 4 + 16 ≤ 3x − x ⟹ 20 ≤ 2x ⟹ x ≥ 10; with x < 15: **{10, 11, 12, 13, 14}**
d) −5x < −3 ⟹ x > [[3/5]]; integers from −3 to 3 greater than 0.6: **{1, 2, 3}**
[[fig:m8-f21]]
Figure 7.2: Solution sets on number lines

pages.title: Exercise 7.3
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 7.3** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
1. List the solution set: a) x + 3 < 9, x ∈ {whole numbers} b) 3x − 1 ≥ 11, x ∈ {integers ≤ 8} c) −2 < x ≤ 3, x ∈ {integers}
2. Solve and show on a number line: a) 5x + 3 > 18 b) 4 − x ≥ 1 c) 2(x + 1) < x + 5
3. A learner has GH₵50 and buys exercise books at GH₵7 each. Write and solve an inequality for the number of books he can buy. List the possible numbers.

pages.title: Chapter 7 summary
pages.body:
- <, >, ≤, ≥ compare quantities; "at least" is ≥, "at most" is ≤.
- Solve like an equation, but reverse the sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative number.
- Open circle: not included; closed circle: included.

questions.q: Solve 12 − 3y ≤ 2y + 2 and give the smallest whole number solution.
Find the integer values of x for which −1 ≤ 2x + 3 < 9.
Ama wants to score an average of at least 70 in three tests. She scored 62 and 75 in the first two. What must she score in the third?
Write an inequality for "a number decreased by 5 is less than twice the number" and solve it.
